brand_001:n1.prompt:
You are helping me generate and evaluate brand-name candidates for my new company. First, ask me for: (1) a short description of what the company does, (2) my target industry/audience, (3) any words, tones, or themes I want included or avoided, and (4) which social platforms matter most to me (e.g., Instagram, X/Twitter, TikTok, LinkedIn).

Once I provide this, generate 15-20 distinct brand-name candidates that fit the business description and tone. For each candidate, do the following checks and record results in a table:

1. Domain availability: check whether the .com (and .io or .co if relevant) version of the name is registered, using a WHOIS lookup or domain registrar search.
2. Social handle availability: check whether the exact name (or close variant) is available as a username on the platforms I specified, by searching each platform directly.
3. Trademark conflict risk: search the USPTO Trademark Electronic Search System (TESS) or an equivalent public trademark database for exact or close matches in my industry class, and note any potential conflicts.

Score each candidate on a simple scale (e.g., green/yellow/red) for each of the three dimensions, then produce an overall ranking with your top 5 recommendations, briefly explaining the reasoning for each (memorability, relevance, risk level).

Done looks like: a clear table of all candidates with domain, social, and trademark status, plus a ranked shortlist of 5 names with rationale.

Report back with the full table, the top 5 shortlist, and any caveats (e.g., searches that were inconclusive or required manual verification). Do not register any domain, handle, or trademark — this is research only.

brand_001:n2.prompt:
You are helping me evaluate brand-name candidates for my new company. Please ask me for: (1) the list of candidate names I want checked, (2) my preferred domain extensions (e.g., .com, .io, .co), (3) the social platforms I care about (e.g., Instagram, X/Twitter, TikTok, LinkedIn, YouTube), and (4) the country/jurisdiction whose trademark register matters most to me (e.g., USPTO for the US, EUIPO for the EU).

For each candidate name, do the following:
1. Domain availability: check the exact name plus close variants across my requested extensions using a WHOIS lookup or a domain registrar's availability search (e.g., via Namecheap or GoDaddy's public search page). Note which extensions are free vs. taken.
2. Social handle availability: visit each requested platform and check whether the exact handle (and one or two close variants) is available or already claimed. Note follower count/activity if the handle is taken, so I can gauge conflict severity.
3. Trademark conflicts: search the relevant trademark office's public database (e.g., USPTO TESS for the US, or the EUIPO database for the EU) for exact and close matches in relevant business categories. Also run a general web search for existing companies using the name to catch unregistered but active conflicts.

Compile a single table with columns: Name | Domain status (per extension) | Social handle status (per platform) | Trademark/usage conflict findings | Overall risk score (low/medium/high) with a one-line rationale.

Done looks like: every candidate has been checked across all three dimensions with sources noted, and the table is complete with an overall risk score for ranking. Report back the full table plus a short summary recommending the top 2-3 names with the fewest conflicts.

brand_001:n3.prompt:
You are helping me pick a company name. Please act as the branding agent for the 'Present ranked candidates' step. If I haven't already given you the inputs, ask me for: (1) a short description of what my company does, (2) any keywords, themes, or style preferences for the name, (3) preferred domain TLDs (e.g. .com, .io), (4) which social platforms matter to me (e.g. X, Instagram, TikTop, LinkedIn), and (5) which country/jurisdiction(s) I care about for trademark risk.

Once you have that, generate 8-12 candidate brand names. For each candidate, check and record: domain availability for my preferred TLDs (use a domain lookup/WHOIS search), handle availability on the social platforms I named (search each platform directly), and potential trademark conflicts (search public trademark databases and general web/business registries for existing uses of the same or confusingly similar name in my industry).

Score each candidate on a simple scale (e.g. 1-5) for domain availability, handle availability, and trademark risk (lower risk = higher score), then compute a composite rank. Present the results as a single ranked table: Name | Domain status | Social handle status | Trademark risk notes | Composite score | Rank.

Below the table, write 2-3 sentences on the top 3 candidates explaining tradeoffs (e.g. strong domain but weak trademark clearance). Do not register any domain, handle, or trademark — just present the ranked findings and ask me which candidate(s) I'd like to move forward with. Report back the full table plus your top-3 recommendation summary.
